tools.name: move_requirements_between_areas
tools.description: Preview or queue a move of requirements, and of Area relation links, to another Area of the same project only. Managers only. Public codes are never reissued; TC results, lifecycle and relationships are preserved. Preview first (dryRun defaults to true) and read newViolations. Apply with the preview token, the latest project writeRevision and a stable client requestId; applying with the token accepts the listed new violations, while duplicate codes, duplicate links and orphan links block. Apply returns an operationId promptly; poll get_move_operation for queued, running, succeeded or failed status and the final moveRunId. A dropped connection does not cancel the operation, and explicit cancellation is not supported.

projectCode.description: Server-generated project public code from list_projects

expectedRevision.description: Latest project writeRevision

previewToken.description: Token returned by preview; required when dryRun is false

requestId.description: Client-generated stable ID for an apply attempt; required when dryRun is false. Reuse it to read or retry the same operation

tools.name: move_tasks_and_testcases
tools.description: Preview or queue a move of TASKs and TCs to another requirement of the same project only. Managers only. Public codes, results, revision history, lifecycle, dependencies and comments are preserved. Codes are never reissued, so a code prefix names the origin, not the current owner. Detailed-requirement (clause) links and TASK-TC links that are not remapped with clauseCodes or testCaseCodes are dropped and listed in droppedLinks; derived status changes are listed in statusChanges and new validation findings in newViolations. Move linked TCs in the same plan through testCases. Preview first (dryRun defaults to true); applying with the preview token, the latest project writeRevision and a stable client requestId accepts the listed drops, status changes and new violations. Duplicate codes and orphan links block. The destination must be a non-deprecated requirement in an active Area. Apply returns an operationId promptly; poll get_move_operation.

instructions:
PDSpec stores SDD projects: Areas contain requirements (REQ), which own TASKs and TCs. Every item has a server-issued public code.
Read before writing. Each write takes expectedRevision from the latest read: the project writeRevision comes from list_projects or get_project_field_schemas, an item's writeRevision from reading that item. A stale value fails with SDD_STALE_WRITE; read again instead of retrying blindly.
Public codes never change and are never reused. After a move, a code's prefix names where the item was created, not where it lives now. Find the current owner with list_tasks (taskCode) or list_testcases (testCaseCode) and read primaryRequirementCode; add lifecycle and areaLifecycle "all" for deprecated items or archived Areas.
To reorganize, never delete and re-create items: re-creation issues new codes and loses results, history, comments and relations. Use move_requirements_between_areas (REQ to another Area), move_tasks_and_testcases (TASK or TC to another REQ) and reorder_areas (Area display order). Moves work within one project and need a manager.
Move flow: preview first (dryRun defaults to true); review droppedLinks, statusChanges and newViolations; keep traceability with clauseCodes and testCaseCodes and move linked TCs in the same plan. Then apply with dryRun false, the same plan and expectedRevision, the previewToken and a stable requestId, and poll get_move_operation until succeeded or failed. After SDD_MOVE_PREVIEW_STALE or SDD_STALE_WRITE, preview again.
Errors carry a stable code; branch on the code, not the message. The pdspec-develop skill from /api/agent-kit describes the full workflow.
